review_locator: PMCID:PMC5124539, Role of Interleukin-18 in the Pathophysiology of Allergic Diseases; PMCID:PMC5920033, Unique Action of Interleukin-18 on T Cells and Other Immune Cells
primary_title: IL-18 and IL-33 elicit Th2 cytokines from basophils via a MyD88- and p38alpha-dependent pathway
decision_basis: The review-guided primary shows IL-18-induced p38alpha phosphorylation in basophils is MyD88-dependent.
limitations_preserved: Preserve mouse basophil and IL-3 co-stimulation context; this is a measured pathway activation bridge with MyD88 dependence, not direct IL-18-to-p38alpha binding, SCI inference or terminal-TF evidence.

decision_basis: The review-guided primary shows IL-18 increases basophil survival together with enhanced Akt activation.

primary_title: IL-18, although antiallergic when administered with IL-12, stimulates IL-4 and histamine release by basophils
decision_basis: The review-guided primary shows IL-18 alone enhances histamine production/release by basophils in wild-type and IFN-gamma-deficient mice.
limitations_preserved: Preserve mouse basophil and in-vivo cytokine context; IL-12 co-administration changes the response, and this mediator-output bridge does not infer direct degranulation machinery, SCI relevance or terminal-TF evidence.
